topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture topic and frames how previously learned immune components fit into the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: They detail how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns, receptor families, and downstream signaling complexes.

topics.label: Inflammatory response, cell recruitment, and systemic complications
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the cellular and vascular events of the acute inflammatory cascade, from leukocyte trafficking and lymphatic drainage to the pathological risks of excessive systemic activation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the processes that shut down acute inflammation, facilitate tissue repair, and manage persistent or chronic inflammatory states.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and indicates the topic of the following session.
